headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Dagster’s no-write/no-network profile is paired with a local RAG agent that reads/writes files, runs shells, and handles secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP bridge, so direct injection paths are absent. The production-agentic-rag-course agent does read files and process notebook/API inputs, so only manual or file-based content transfer could carry instructions. That makes the pathway possible but unusual and limited.
conditions: IF operator manually copies Dagster output into the RAG agent's prompt or notebook cells, injected instructions can be executed as text.
IF a shared file is introduced between the two agents, file content can become an instruction carrier.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into the RAG agent.
Add a fixed prompt prefix that labels Dagster output as untrusted.
Review any shared notebook cells before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while the RAG agent touches academic papers, metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets and can read/write local files. If they share a workspace, the RAG agent can ingest files that Dagster or its operators place there, creating a realistic leakage path in default local-development setups.
conditions: IF both agents are run in the same local directory, files written by the operator or surrounding tooling can be read by the RAG agent.
IF secrets are stored in files accessible to the RAG agent, those secrets can be exposed in its outputs.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory.
Move secrets out of shared files before running the pair.
Mount the RAG agent workspace read-only where possible.
Audit the files visible to the RAG agent before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or use the network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. The RAG agent can write files and spawn subprocesses, but without Dagster write access there is no meaningful direct conflict between the pair beyond ordinary operator coordination.
conditions: IF Dagster is wrapped by external tooling that grants it write access not shown in the profile, write conflicts could emerge.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through the operator, the RAG agent may overwrite shared artifacts.
mitigations: Keep Dagster read-only.
Use separate output directories.
Avoid sharing git worktrees between the agents.
Run one agent at a time when editing shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator and the RAG agent exposes ask/agentic-ask endpoints plus notebook-driven workflows, so outputs from one can plausibly feed the other. Because the RAG agent can act on retrieved content and Dagster can orchestrate pipelines, unverified text can cascade into downstream actions unless an explicit verification step is inserted.
conditions: IF Dagster schedules or passes generated text into the RAG agent without validation, errors can propagate.
IF the RAG agent uses retrieved answers as authoritative inputs to later notebook or API steps, incorrect facts can be operationalized.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream actions.
Require schema validation on all inter-agent payloads.
Log and diff intermediate outputs before execution.
Mark Dagster-produced text as untrusted in prompts.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source with no touched data classes listed, while the RAG agent explicitly handles configuration secrets and uses local-development Docker/Airflow credentials. That creates a compliance mismatch around secret handling and retention, even though no PHI or EU residency issue is evidenced. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair's combined handling of sensitive operational data.
conditions: IF configuration secrets are stored in the same workspace as Dagster artifacts, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF the pair is run under a shared operator account, secret handling obligations can be blurred.
mitigations: Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Delete example credential files after setup.
Separate operational logs from content outputs.
Review retention settings for notebooks and pipeline logs.
